"'''End of the Road'''" is a song by American [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]] group [[Boyz II Men]] for the [[Boomerang (soundtrack)|''Boomerang'' soundtrack]]. It was released in June 1992 by [[LaFace Records|LaFace]], [[Arista Records|Arista]] and [[Motown]], and is written by [[Babyface (musician)|Babyface]], Antonio [[L.A. Reid]] and [[Daryl Simmons]].  The song achieved domestic and international success. In the United States, it spent a then record breaking 13 weeks at number one on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], a record broken later in the year by [[Whitney Houston]]'s 14-week number one hit "[[I Will Always Love You (Whitney Houston recording)|I Will Always Love You]]"; Boyz II Men would later match Houston's record with "[[I'll Make Love to You]]", which spent 14 weeks at number one in 1994, and then reclaim the record with "[[One Sweet Day]]" (a duet with [[Mariah Carey]]), which spent 16 weeks at number one from 1995 to 1996.

"End of the Road" was the number one single of 1992 on the ''Billboard'' [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 1992|Year-End Hot 100 Singles of 1992]]. It was also ranked by ''Billboard'' as the sixth most successful song of the decade 1990–1999.<ref name="1990sbb">{{cite book | author = Geoff Mayfield | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=9w0EAAAAMBAJ&pg=RA1-PA4 | title = 1999 The Year in Music Totally '90s: Diary of a Decade - The listing of Top Pop Albums of the '90s & Hot 100 Singles of the '90s | publisher = [[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] | date = December 25, 1999 | access-date = October 15, 2010}}</ref> Internationally, it reached number one in Australia, the United Kingdom and on the [[European Hot 100 Singles|Hot 100 Eurochart]], among others. The music video for the song was directed by [[Lionel C. Martin]].<ref name="imvdb">{{Cite web|title=Boys II Men - End Of The Road (1993)|url=https://imvdb.com/video/boyz-ii-men/end-of-the-road|access-date=2024-02-25|publisher=IMVDb}}</ref><ref name="imdb">{{Cite web|title=Boys II Men: End of the Road (1993)|url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt7085420/|access-date=2024-02-25|publisher=[[IMDb]]}}</ref> "End of the Road" has been certified Platinum by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] for shipments of over one million units in the United States.<ref name="US Certification">{{cite web |url=http://riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?resultpage=1&table=SEARCH_RESULTS&action=&title=End_of_the_Road&artist=&format=&debutLP=&category=&sex=&releaseDate=&requestNo=&type=&level=&label=&company=&certificationDate=&awardDescription=&catalogNo=&aSex=&rec_id=&charField=&gold=&platinum=&multiPlat=&level2=&certDate=&album=&id=&after=&before=&startMonth=1&endMonth=1&startYear=1958&endYear=2009&sort=Artist&perPage=10 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120713113436/http://riaa.com/goldandplatinumdata.php?resultpage=1&table=SEARCH_RESULTS&action=&title=End_of_the_Road&artist=&format=&debutLP=&category=&sex=&releaseDate=&requestNo=&type=&level=&label=&company=&certificationDate=&awardDescription=&catalogNo=&aSex=&rec_id=&charField=&gold=&platinum=&multiPlat=&level2=&certDate=&album=&id=&after=&before=&startMonth=1&endMonth=1&startYear=1958&endYear=2009&sort=Artist&perPage=10 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-07-13 |title=RIAA - Certified Awards Search - "End of the Road"]. |publisher=[[Recording Industry Association of America|RIAA]] |access-date=2014-11-28 }}</ref> The song also won [[Grammy Award for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals|Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-12-10 |title=GRAMMY Rewind: Watch Boyz II Men Win GRAMMY For Best R&B Performance By A Duo Or Group For "End Of The Road" In 1993 |url=https://grammy.com/news/grammy-rewind-watch-boyz-ii-men-win-best-performance-duo-or-group-end-of-the-road-1993 |access-date=2025-06-13 |website=Grammy}}</ref> and [[Grammy Award for Best R&B Song|Best R&B Song]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=35th Annual GRAMMY Awards {{!}} GRAMMY.com |url=https://grammy.com/awards/35th-annual-grammy-awards |access-date=2025-06-13 |website=Grammy}}</ref> at the [[35th Annual Grammy Awards|1993 Grammy Awards]].

"End of the Road" is a song by American R&B group Boyz II Men for the Boomerang soundtrack. It was released in June 1992 by LaFace, Arista and Motown, and is written by Babyface, Antonio L.A. Reid and Daryl Simmons.  The song achieved domestic and international success. In the United States, it spent a then record breaking 13 weeks at number one on the US Billboard Hot 100, a record broken later in the year by Whitney Houston's 14-week number one hit "I Will Always Love You"; Boyz II Men would later match Houston's record with "I'll Make Love to You", which spent 14 weeks at number one in 1994, and then reclaim the record with "One Sweet Day" (a duet with Mariah Carey), which spent 16 weeks at number one from 1995 to 1996.

"End of the Road" was the number one single of 1992 on the Billboard Year-End Hot 100 Singles of 1992. It was also ranked by Billboard as the sixth most successful song of the decade 1990–1999. Internationally, it reached number one in Australia, the United Kingdom and on the Hot 100 Eurochart, among others. The music video for the song was directed by Lionel C. Martin. "End of the Road" has been certified Platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America for shipments of over one million units in the United States. The song also won Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals and Best R&B Song at the 1993 Grammy Awards.

sections.heading: Release and chart performance
sections.wikitext:
"End of the Road" was released on June 30, 1992.{{citation needed|date=September 2025}} It was released as a single from the ''Boomerang'' [[soundtrack]] and did not originally appear on Boyz II Men's debut album, ''[[Cooleyhighharmony]]''. It was released after all singles from their debut had been released, and was their fifth single overall. However, ''Cooleyhighharmony'' was re-issued in 1992 and 1993 to include "End of the Road" due to the success of the single. In 1993 the Spanish version of the song ″Al Final Del Camino″ was released as a single alongside producer Rex Salas.

The single debuted at number 53 on the US ''Billboard'' Hot 100 on July 18, 1992, jumping to number 30 the following week. The next week the song reached the top ten at number eight, and reached the top five the week after at number four. The following week, the song peaked at number one, holding the position for 13 consecutive weeks from August 15, 1992 to November 7, 1992. On November 14, the song was finally succeeded by "[[How Do You Talk to an Angel]]" by [[The Heights (American TV series)|the Heights]]. It also spent four weeks atop of the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|''Billboard'' Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart]].

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: The song is written and composed in the [[Key (music)|key]] of [[E-flat major|E{{music|flat}} major]] and its relative key, [[C minor]] (for the pre-choruses)<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Kenneth "Babyface" |first1=Edmonds |last2=A |first2=Reid, L. |last3=Daryl |first3=Simmons |last4=Men |first4=Boyz II |last5=Kenneth "Babyface" |first5=Edmonds |date=1999-12-15 |title=End of the Road |url=https://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtd.asp?ppn=MN0026762 |access-date=2026-10-12 |website=Musicnotes.com}}</ref> and is set in [[time signature]] of {{music|time|12|8}} with a [[tempo]] of 50 beats per minute. The group members' vocals span from E{{music|flat}}<sub>3</sub> to C<sub>5</sub>.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: [[Larry Flick]] from ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine commented, "Good to hear something new by this wonderfully talented group." He described the song as a "retrominded [[R&B-Pop|pop/R&B]] tune", noting that "those now-recognizable harmonies glide over a swaying, [[doo-wop]] melody, making the track the perfect complement to a romantic evening. Has the markings of a major multiformat smash."<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Larry |last= Flick |title= Single Reviews |magazine= [[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date= July 18, 1992 |page= 72 |access-date= October 25, 2020 |url= https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-Billboard/90s/1992/Billboard-1992-07-18.pdf |author-link= Larry Flick}}</ref> British magazine ''[[Music Week]]'' wrote, "A superior if stylised [[ballad]], with some classically soulful crooning and a smoothly polished finish, it looks set for major success here too. Cute acapella end adds to appeal."<ref>{{cite magazine|url= https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-Week/1992/MW-1992-08-29.pdf |title= Mainstream: Singles |magazine= [[Music Week]] |date= August 29, 1992 |page= 6 |access-date= October 2, 2020}}</ref> Jonathan Bernstein from ''[[Spin (magazine)|Spin]]'' called it "lugubrious".<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Jonathan|last=Bernstein|title=The Year In Pop|magazine=[[Spin (magazine)|Spin]]|date=December 1992|page=42|accessdate=January 25, 2023|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uZFqiGmZIPAC}}</ref> In 2024, ''[[Forbes]]'' magazine ranked "End of the Road" number 38 in their list of "The 50 Best Songs of the 1990s", naming it "a soulful ballad that captured the pain of heartbreak and loss."<ref>{{cite web|first=Hugh|last=McIntyre|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/entertainment/article/best-90s-songs/|title=The 50 Best Songs Of The 1990s|work=[[Forbes]]|date=March 9, 2024|access-date=March 1, 2025}}</ref> In 2025, ''Billboard'' ranked it number 16 in their "Top 100 Breakup Songs of All Time" list, writing that the "buttery group vocals nail the "unnatural" post-breakup feeling of being apart from someone who still feels painfully familiar to you."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Hannah|last=Dailey|url=https://www.billboard.com/lists/top-breakup-songs-all-time/boyz-ii-men-end-of-the-road/|title=Top 100 Breakup Songs of All Time|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=February 11, 2025|access-date=April 14, 2025}}</ref>

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The accompanying music video for "End of the Road" was directed by American music video director, film director and VJ [[Lionel C. Martin]].<ref name="imvdb"/><ref name="imdb"/> It was made in both black-and-white and colors, featuring Boyz II Men performing the song while sitting on chairs in a room, standing outside a train station, or walking in a hallway, interspersed with scenes from the movie ''Boomerang''. The video was later made available in remastered HD on the group's official [[YouTube]] channel in 2009, and had generated almost 300 million views in early 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Boys II Men - End Of The Road|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zDKO6XYXioc|date=2009-12-25|access-date=2024-02-25|publisher=[[YouTube]]}}</ref>
sections.text: The accompanying music video for "End of the Road" was directed by American music video director, film director and VJ Lionel C. Martin. It was made in both black-and-white and colors, featuring Boyz II Men performing the song while sitting on chairs in a room, standing outside a train station, or walking in a hallway, interspersed with scenes from the movie Boomerang. The video was later made available in remastered HD on the group's official YouTube channel in 2009, and had generated almost 300 million views in early 2024.

sections.heading: Covers
sections.wikitext: The song has been covered by various artists both domestically and internationally including the Korean group [[BTS]]<ref>"The end of Taehyung’s 210724 먹방 Vlive featuring Namjoon". Boyz II Men’s “End of the Road”. July 24, 2021. [July 24, 2021. [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PDoHS-JTWSI]</ref> and the ''[[a cappella]]'' country group [[Home Free (group)|Home Free]].<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-lCRFAFtj-A "Boyz II Men - End of the Road (Home Free Cover)". Jan 11, 2019]</ref> and a punk rock group, [[Me First and the Gimme Gimmes]] on their fourth album, ''Take a Break''.
sections.text: The song has been covered by various artists both domestically and internationally including the Korean group BTS and the a cappella country group Home Free. and a punk rock group, Me First and the Gimme Gimmes on their fourth album, Take a Break.

sections.heading: In popular culture
sections.wikitext: In 2026, the song was parodied in a commercial for ''[[Old Spice]]''<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZX5gTtTggOE Mom Song: The End of Adolescents | Old Spice]</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Watson |first1=Imogen |url=https://adweek.com/creativity/old-spice-updates-mom-song-with-a-modern-motherhood-twist/ |title=Old Spice Updates 'Mom Song' With a Modern Motherhood Twist |website=adweek |access-date=2026-02-13 |date=February 13, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Orosa |first1=Roberto |url=https://news.designrush.com/old-spice-wieden-kennedy-mom-song-swagger-campaign |title=Old Spice Reworks a Boys II Men Classic for a Coming-of-Age Campaign |website=designrush |access-date=2026-02-13 |date=February 13, 2026}}</ref>as "Mom Song: The End of Adolescents".
sections.text: In 2026, the song was parodied in a commercial for Old Spiceas "Mom Song: The End of Adolescents".
